tasks.notes: plan-defect: the fifth GLOBAL CONSTRAINT states the block is "under 24 KB however many failures the run recorded", but the only quantities bounded are the row count (FACTS_MAX_ROWS = 20, fleet/facts-block.mjs:77,142) and each evidence field (FACTS_FIELD_MAX = 500, fleet/facts-block.mjs:80,105-108). rowLine (fleet/facts-block.mjs:117) renders `row.paths.join(', ')` — the row's entire path list, unbounded in count and length. At the bound, 20 rows already spend ~20,000 characters on read+against plus ~1.6 KB of fixed per-row text and ~200 characters of header, leaving under ~2 KB for every path of every row. A `driver:finding` whose detail names no path carries the task's whole touch set (Task 3 M1), so a many-file task can push a single row's path join past that alone and the block over 24 KB. The fix is not available inside this task's FILES: M2 spells the row line as `[<paths joined by ', '>]` — the row's own paths, all of them, which is also the reading the exam pins byte-for-byte at fleet/tests/test_facts_block.mjs:452-463 — so capping the rendered list here would contradict the Machine clause the diff was graded on. Settling it means amending M2 (a per-row path budget, or a tail elision) or restating the constraint's arithmetic to bound only the evidence fields. Nothing in this submission is wrong against its own task text; recording it so the operator can decide before Task 5 wires the block into a brief.

Code quality, `examReceiptOf` in `fleet/run-engine.mjs`: `paths` is built as `[...landings, ...files].map(String).filter(Boolean)`, so the `String` conversion runs *before* the truthiness filter. `landingOf` (fleet/run-engine.mjs:2488) returns `undefined` whenever a factsheet is present and its `landing` map has no entry for a Proof path — `String(undefined)` is the non-empty string `'undefined'`, which survives `.filter(Boolean)` and lands in the record as a repo-relative path that does not exist. Filtering first also keeps the Context slot's shared literal honest on the other edge (`paths` "never empty"): with both lists empty the current code silently yields `[]`. Neither case is reachable in the sims (leg (b)'s task has no factsheet and `examRunnable` requires `proofTests.length`), so the exam is green either way — this is a defensive one-liner, not a failing leg.; unverified: the GLOBAL CONSTRAINT "Every new event kind and every new event field is named in `fleet/CONTRACT.md`" cannot be settled by this diff — the fields it adds (`paths` and `evidence` on `driver:exam-run` and on `resolver:reply`) are new event fields, and `fleet/CONTRACT.md` is outside this task's FILES (it is sibling task 6's, popmechanic-ultrapowers#1csr). The constraint carries no `Check:` the driver ran, so this is prose-grounded and minor. What settles it: I read `fleet/CONTRACT.md` in the integration clone and its Receipts paragraph (lines 124-131) already names the receipt literal and lists `driver:exam-run` (red rows only) and `resolver:reply` (rows whose status is not `RESOLVED`) among the kinds that carry one — i.e. the constraint is satisfied in the integrated tree by task 6, and nothing is owed inside this task's footprint. Recorded so the operator sees the dependency, not as work for a fix round.; concern: out-of-FILES (not taken): fleet/CONTRACT.md — the Global Constraint "Every new event kind and every new event field is named in fleet/CONTRACT.md" is now owed two entries this task's code created: the `paths` and `evidence` fields on `driver:exam-run`, and the fact that `resolver:reply` is a row the wave loop actually writes (the contract lists the kind only among those the status projection skips). fleet/CONTRACT.md is Task 6's declared file, so the edit was not mine to land.

Duplicate module-level declarations after the fold: this task's `fleet/run-engine.mjs` hunk adds `export const receiptText` and `export const receiptPaths` (patch lines 16-24, just below `touchSetOf`), and sibling Task 2 — whose Interfaces slot is contracted to Produce exactly `receiptPaths(list)` from this same file — adds `export const receiptPaths`, `export const RECEIPT_TEXT_MAX` and `export const receiptText` in a different region of the file (task-2.patch lines 104-110; already present in the integration tree at fleet/run-engine.mjs:817-828). The two hunks are far apart, so git folds both cleanly and the folded module carries two module-scope `const receiptPaths` and two `const receiptText` — `SyntaxError: Identifier 'receiptPaths' has already been declared`, plus duplicate export names, which takes the whole engine and every sim with it. This task's Interfaces say `Produces: none` and `Consumes: none` (rule 4), so it was neither entitled to mint these exports nor able to import the sibling's; the lawful shape is file-private helpers under names no sibling claims. The exam and the Run: evidence are green only because task 3's clone is folded alone. Fix inside this task's own FILES: rename the three helpers and drop `export` (the added exam does not import them, and nothing in the plan references `receiptEvidence` or `pathTokensIn`).

fleet/publish-fold.mjs is wired whole (commit 0af83fde, +98/-36): `onEvent: eventLog.onEvent` on the resolveConflicts call, both `driver:publish-fold` appends through `publishFoldEvent(row, conflictsIndex())`, `writeResolverBriefs` taking `receipts` and appending `factsBlock(receipts, [conflict.path])`, `receiptRows(<runDir>/events.jsonl)` read once at attempt start, and one `driver:facts` row per non-empty brief. Drove a real fold (bare origin, full clone, canned resolver) and measured every leg: (b) and (d) are green in full, (a) is green but for the resolver:reply row's `paths`/`evidence`, (c) is green but renders one `- receipt` line instead of two. Both reds are the same missing edge — the `resolver:reply` row is built in `resolveConflicts` in fleet/run-engine.mjs, which is Task 1's file (popmechanic-ultrapowers#d56q) and at BASE emits {kind,label,conflict,attempt,status} only. Filed blocked-by #d56q; work.attention is stuck. Nothing else here changes once Task 1 folds in.

`renderedReceiptIds` is added as a module-level `export` (fleet/run-engine.mjs:1286) but nothing imports it — the only caller is `factsFor` a few hundred lines below, in the same module. The task's Interfaces name exactly one Produces symbol, `waveContendingBlock`; exporting a second helper widens the engine's public surface past what the task declares, and past what either Proof `Test:` path pins (`test_resolver_brief.mjs` asserts only `waveContendingBlock`). Dropping the `export` keeps the Produces contract the one the task named.; The wave loop's `contendingBlock` wrapper (fleet/run-engine.mjs:4066-4075) renders the block once via `blockForConflict(conflict)` and then asks `factsFor` for the same query a second time, re-deriving the conflict path with a second copy of `String((conflict && conflict.path) || '')` — the same expression `waveContendingBlock` already carries at line 50 of the patch. The comment argues the two answers cannot differ, which is true today, but it is two spellings of one path rule and two renders of one block; if either side's path derivation is ever changed the `driver:facts` row would silently name rows the resolver never read. The block the wrapper already holds is enough: `if (block) appendEvent({ kind: 'driver:facts', label: 'resolve:wave' + waveNumber + ':' + conflict.i, receipts: renderedReceiptIds(block) })` records exactly the rendered rows without a second query, which is the same invariant `factsFor` was built to hold for the examiner and reviewer.; `renderedReceiptIds` (fleet/run-engine.mjs:1286-1293) recovers ids by splitting the rendered block on `\n` and matching `/^- receipt (\S+) /` per physical line, but `factsBlock`'s `field()` bounds a receipt's `read`/`against` to 500 characters without stripping newlines, and two receipt kinds put freeform worker text there — `resolverReceiptOf` renders a resolver's `notes` into `read`, and `driver:finding` renders a review block's `detail`. A receipt whose evidence text happens to contain a line beginning `- receipt <token> ` would put a phantom id into the `driver:facts` row's `receipts`, which is the array the operator's pre-registered reading is counted from. This is record-row noise only — the judge's own brief is unaffected — but anchoring the match to the full row shape (id, kind and the `[` that opens the paths list, e.g. `/^- receipt (\S+) \S+ \[/`) removes the class.
